There are two approaches depending on your access level.

## Option 1: Search API (recommended for admins)

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/search/v1
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.email:\"jane.doe@example.com\""
  }
}
```

The search API accepts Elasticsearch-style queries and returns full identity objects. Note that search results have a short ingestion lag (seconds to minutes) relative to the operational database.

## Option 2: Public Identities API (works for non-admins too)

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/public-identities/v1?filters=email eq "jane.doe@example.com"
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

The docs explicitly show this filter pattern. It returns only the attributes your org has marked as publicly visible, so it may have fewer fields than the search result. If the email address contains special characters, URL-encode spaces as `%20` and double-quotes as `%22`.

## Authentication

For either call, first obtain an access token via the Client Credentials grant:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="{clientId}"' \
  --form 'client_secret="{clientSecret}"'
```

Then pass the returned `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}` on every subsequent request.

**Which to use:** Use the Search API if you need full identity data and have admin-level access. Use Public Identities if you only need publicly visible attributes or are operating under a non-admin user context.

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: POST
    path: /search/v1
    api_version: search/v1
  - method: GET
    path: /public-identities/v1
    api_version: public-identities/v1
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [indices, query, filters]
```
